memo.argument: Heading 3921 covers 'Other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics' that are reinforced with materials other than plastic or are cellular. The product is a laminated composite of PET (polyethylene terephthalate) and polyethylene film—two different plastic materials bonded together. Under GRI 3(b), composite goods are classified by the material giving them essential character. Both materials are plastics, making this a plastic-to-plastic laminate. The heading text of 3921 explicitly covers 'plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics' and includes laminated structures. The product qualifies as a laminated plastic film under 3921. The best 10-digit code is 3921.90.40.90 (Other: Flexible: Other), which covers flexible plastic films of other plastics not otherwise specified. The laminated structure and packaging function support classification in 3921 rather than 3920, which is limited to noncellular plastics 'not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials'—a heading that would exclude multi-layer plastic composites.
exclusions_against: Heading 3920 explicitly states 'noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials,' which excludes laminated plastic-to-plastic composites. Ruling N331595 and N351059 both hold that plastic films laminated to other plastic materials are excluded from 3921 and classified in 3920 instead, directly contradicting the argument for 3921. Ruling N351059 specifically states: 'Heading 3921 covers plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics that have been reinforced with materials other than plastic. As this product is constructed entirely of plastic layers it is excluded from classification in 3921.90.4090.'

events.text: {"heading":"8479","best_code":"8479.89.95.00","argument":"A home beer dispenser designed to dispense bottled beer using a hand-operated valve and compressed CO2 is a machine and mechanical appliance having an individual function not specified or included elsewhere in Chapter 84.
